newsitem.title: JAPAN: No Thai requests yet for help--Japan's Mitsuzuka.
newsitem.headline: No Thai requests yet for help--Japan's Mitsuzuka.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Friday that there have been no specific requests from the Thai government for Japan to help with its financial problems.
"There have been no concrete requests yet about support," Mitsuzuka told a regular news conference.
He said his ministry is currently trying to set up a meeting with the Thai finance minister, who is scheduled to visit Japan next week.
"If he comes to Japan I am sure we will meet," Mitsuzuka said.
He said he welcomes the Thai decision to float its baht and Bangkok's efforts to stabilise its economy. He added that the International Monetary Fund also supported the Thai efforts.

Asked about IMF support for the Philippines, he said: "I just heard about it after returning from the cabinet meeting (on Friday morning). Right now, I have instructed ministry officials to analyse the information," he said.
Mitsuzuka also said that Asian currencies were likely to head toward stability.

Asked if the present instability of Asian currencies may lead to further confusion similar to the Mexican peso crisis of 1994, he said: "Currencies move on various factors. We must look at the overall picture, but I think they will head in the direction of settling down."
Japan, as the leading economy in Asia, will keep in close touch with other Asian countries to help achieve stability in their currencies, he said.
